pairs.difference: A: the saloon walls, gable board, posts and sand all sit in one orange-to-cream family, the windows are amber, and only the sky breaks it, so warm share is 0.786, above the real range. In the lens the building is three steps of orange-tan with no neutral. B: the night motel has a dominant blue field, a pink and green sign and mauve-brown posts, so its hues play separate roles and its warm share is 0.363.
pairs.fix: Paint the saloon boards in greyed, weathered brown and the wall panels in cool off-white, with blue-grey in the shadows. Keep orange only on the lit windows.

pairs.difference: B: the parchment is peach-cream on a saturated blue table and backdrop, with no grey anywhere, and the red and gold seal is the only accent. Warm share 0.211 is below range and shadow chroma 1.419 is above it, so the shade stays as colorful as the lit side. A: the cart's rust brown, grey iron rims and sand give believable local colors, and the steel rests the eye.
pairs.fix: Make the paper a cooler ivory that turns soft grey-lilac in the shadow of the roll, and lower the blue of the table and wall.

pairs.difference: B: a full-strength violet field (background chroma 0.2635, far above the real 0.217 top) sits behind a yellow-gold star, with the ruby as the only other hue. Nothing neutral rests the eye, and hero and ground are equally loud. A: the box mixes crimson with beige cushion and a blue ribbon on cyan rays, and the cushion gives real muted area. Its 5.43 hue families run slightly high, but the masses keep distinct roles.
pairs.fix: Dull the purple background to a deeper, less pure violet with darker rays, and let the gold star fall to a brownish olive in its shaded facets.

pairs.difference: B: the wood floor and walls are all red-orange brown, and even the white cap crown reads cream-tan in the lens, as in the generated lessons where whites drift warm. Warm share 0.85 is above range and background chroma 0.0853 is below it, so the card is warm and flat with no cool relief except the navy. A: the navy cap with violet shading and a thin gold accent sits on clean cyan rings, with a clear hue split between hero and ground.
pairs.fix: Keep the cap crown a clean white with blue-lilac shadows. Make the wood a greyer, less orange brown, and add cool light to the wall.

pairs.difference: A: pure blue door, orange frame, green ivy and a multicolor wreath, all at similar high chroma but each in a believable local color. B: taupe-grey wood and silver blades (subject chroma 0.0316, below range) against blue sky and yellow-green grass, with a single red vane accent. B's grey is like the real cards' neutrals, and A's loudness matches real cards. Neither card gives a directional color tell.

B: golden-orange branches on peach sand take up the whole lower card, shadows stay red-brown or magenta, and the only other hue is the purple wall, so there is no neutral at all and hue families sit at the 2.96 low edge. Background chroma 0.1791 also touches the top of the range. A: red and gold cart, but white awning stripes, pale pavers and glass give the eye resting neutrals against the blue.
pairs.fix: Paint the twigs in dry grey-brown wood with some pale bleached sticks. Make the sand a paler, less orange tan, and give the shadow a cool grey-violet.

pairs.difference: A: blue-grey steel sits on a pure lime field (background chroma 0.2258, above range) with only small gold rivets, giving 1.29 hue families, below range. The ground is much louder than the hero and the palette is thin. B: the cobalt pillow turns cyan on top and violet in its folds on soft pink, so the shadows stay rich and related and the hero leads. Low steel chroma alone is expected on real metal, so this call is weak.
pairs.fix: Deepen the green background to a less neon grass green with darker edges, and let the steel pick up a little warm brass reflection.

pairs.difference: A: pink roses and green leaves on pastel pink stripes, with brown-grey lattice as a neutral. B: red-brown piano on cyan stripes with an orange floor, and the white keys go cool in the lens. Both have backgrounds below the real range (0.0954 and 0.1191) and shadows near the low end, so the numbers do not separate them. Local colors are believable on both.

B: crimson walls, a terracotta plinth, a gold plaque and a cream column make warm share 0.962, well above range, and the marble has drifted to butter-cream as whites do in the generated lessons. Its mauve volute shadow is still related, so the tell is the warm pull rather than the shade. A: gold on violet with a teal cloth, loud (background 0.1994, just over range), but it has a true warm/cool split and warm share 0.234.
pairs.fix: Make the column cool stone white with grey-blue shadows, and shift the wall to a cooler wine or blue-violet so that the card is not entirely red and cream.

pairs.difference: B: neon green collar, teal laces, magenta and orange sole accents and blue mesh all crowd one small hero, on a yellow-orange ground, for 5.49 hue families, above range. There are too many accents competing and no single one leads. A: one cobalt body with a black handle and white rim on pink over orange wood, so the hero is one hue with clear roles, even though subject chroma 0.1653 runs a little high.
pairs.fix: Reduce the sneakers to blue with white soles and one accent color. Remove the rainbow laces and multicolored sole patches.

pairs.difference: B: the scarf is a single pure red (subject chroma 0.2165, above the 0.189 top) with crimson folds, on bright cyan swirls, so the hero is pushed to maximum hue with no duller local cloth color. A: the steel is near neutral with a warm taupe reflection on amber waves, and the small red end caps are the single accent. Warm share of 1.0 is high, but the grey body rests the eye like real metal cards.
pairs.fix: Make the scarf a slightly deeper, cooler crimson cloth with muted wine shadows, and lower the cyan so the background stays behind it.

pairs.difference: A: the amber wall, orange wood and cream-pink cards are all pulled one way, warm share is 1.0 and hue families 2.68 is below range. The cast shadow goes saturated red-brown, and shadow chroma of 2.216 is far above the real top of 1.308, which is the orange/red shadow fault. B: the sand is warm too, but the ball has blue, green and red panels and lilac-grey shading on white, which gives a cool counterweight.
pairs.fix: Keep the cards white with faint grey-blue shading. Make the table a darker, greyer brown, and paint the cast shadow in a muted cool brown instead of orange-red.

pattern: Across the lessons, generated cards lean warm on neutrals: whites drift to cream or peach, wood and leather go orange, and shadows stay saturated red-orange instead of turning grey, lilac or blue. Backgrounds run cleaner and louder, so hero and ground compete with little muted area. Real cards keep cooler, duller neutrals (grey-lilac on white, blue-grey on metal) and deeper, more muted reds and browns. Smaller tells in the test pairs are one family filling the whole card, or too many accent hues crowded onto one object.
